description:
PLAN.md:82-86 documents the deliberate choice: 'There is no public Resource
trait or struct — the abstraction is documentation-only per the RFC and
inheritance is irrelevant on the wire.'

This is a design choice with a real caller-side cost. RFC 9553 §1.4.4 defines
the abstract Resource type with shared fields (@type, kind, uri, mediaType,
contexts, pref, label) inherited by Calendar (§2.4.1), CryptoKey (§2.6.1),
Directory (§2.6.2), Link (§2.6.3), and Media (§2.6.4). A consumer that wants
to write fn fmt_resource_label(r: &impl Resource) -> String to render any
of the five types uniformly cannot do so. They have to either:

- Match on each concrete type via an outer enum they define themselves.
- Copy-paste the five impls.
- Use serde_json::Value or a private trait they cannot extend.

The wire-format-flat justification ('inheritance is irrelevant on the wire')
addresses serialization but not caller-side ergonomics. A sealed Resource
trait with field accessors costs nothing on the wire and lets consumers write
generic helpers.

Possible shapes:

(a) pub trait Resource { fn uri(&self) -> Option<&str>; fn kind(&self) -> ... }
    with impls for the five types. Trait is sealed via a private super-trait
    so consumers cannot impl it for their own types. Non-breaking to add.
(b) An enum ResourceRef<'a> { Calendar(&'a Calendar), CryptoKey(&'a CryptoKey),
    ... } with From impls. Lets consumers match generically.

The status quo defense — 'callers can write the enum themselves' — is true,
and every consumer of this crate (jmap-contacts-types, jmap-contacts-server,
any third-party) will. The cost is paid five times, not once, and the
abstractions diverge.

If keeping status quo, document the decision on the README. Right now it is
only in PLAN.md, which most callers will not read.
title: No public Resource trait or generic — five Resource-derived types prevent generic 'process any resource' functions
